CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

CVE-2026-8149 is a local availability issue in Bouncy Castle BC-FIPS 2.1.0-2.1.2 affecting specific CPU instruction sets (AVX, AVX-512f) on Linux x86_64. bc-fips 2.1.2 is bundled in the eclipse-temurin FIPS JRE as a transitive dependency required for FIPS 140-3 compliance (CMVP #4943). No upstream fix is available; the FIPS module certification requires bc-fips 2.1.0, and the JRE vendor has not released a patched version. The vulnerability requires local access and affects only the GCM cipher mode implementation. Stargate FIPS variants inherit this dependency from the certified JRE and cannot independently upgrade bc-fips without breaking FIPS compliance. Tracking upstream eclipse-temurin for a certified update that resolves CVE-2026-8149 while maintaining CMVP #4943 certification.

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.

The stargate FIPS variant pulls Bouncy Castle bc-fips 2.1.2 via the shared image/.bouncycastle.inc.yaml fragment (BCFIPS_VERSION). No upstream fix is available: Maven Central currently publishes no release beyond 2.1.2 and the GHSA advisory records first_patched_version as null. The flaw is in the AVX-widened GCM pipelines (gcm128w/gcm512w) on x86_64 hosts and impacts availability only. Remediation requires upstream Bouncy Castle to ship a patched 2.x release. The non-FIPS runtime variant does not include bc-fips and is not affected.

CVE-2022-1471 is exploited via snakeyaml's default Constructor, which deserializes arbitrary Java types from untrusted YAML input and can lead to remote code execution. Bumping to snakeyaml 2.x (the fix) is not possible: Cassandra 4.0 depends on the CustomClassLoaderConstructor(Class, ClassLoader) constructor that was removed in snakeyaml 2.x, so the upgrade breaks DatabaseDescriptor.daemonInitialization(). However, Cassandra 4.0 already applied the runtime mitigation in CASSANDRA-18150 ('Switch to snakeyaml's SafeConstructor'). Its YamlConfigurationLoader constructs config via a SafeConstructor subclass, which rejects tagged types and blocks the RCE exploit path. The only YAML loaded by the Stargate coordinator is operator-controlled config under /stargate/ (stargate-config.yaml, cassandra.yaml, per-module configs); no untrusted YAML deserialization occurs. The vulnerable code path is therefore not in the execute path.

Stargate is currently pinned to Java 8 by its maven-enforcer rule. Will bump to 1.5.x when stargate supports Java 11+. Severity is LOW (CVSS 1.8); exploit requires local high-privilege access.

statements.action_statement: Marked 'not fixed' for the Jetty 9.4.x line (affected range <=9.4.58). No upstream backport planned — 9.4.x is at end-of-life. Severity is LOW (CVSS 3.7).

Fix is only in Jetty 12.0.12. No backport to the 9.4.x line. Upgrading to Jetty 12 requires Java 17 and source changes in stargate (jetty-servlet was moved to org.eclipse.jetty.ee10:jetty-ee10-servlet). Will not be patched until stargate supports Jetty 12.

statements.status_notes: Fixed version Jetty 9.4.60 has not been published to Maven Central. Latest available 9.4.x is 9.4.58.v20250814 (Aug 2025). Moving to Jetty 10+/12 is blocked by Java-version and artifact-rename constraints; will bump to 9.4.60 as soon as it is released.
Duplicate of CVE-2023-2976 (both affect Files.createTempDir()). See that entry for upgrade blocker.

Fixed in guava 32.0.0+. Bumping to 32.1.3-jre via parent dependencyManagement was attempted but fails at runtime: maven-bundle-plugin does not re-embed the sister artifact com.google.guava:failureaccess into the persistence-cassandra-4.0 OSGi bundle after the version override, causing Cassandra's Memtable flush to NoClassDefFoundError on InternalFutureFailureAccess. Will revisit when bundle embedding can be resolved or when stargate moves off maven-bundle-plugin 5.x.
